## Setup

```{r load-data}
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(MuMIn)        # R-squared values for lmer models
library(performance)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

folder <- ""
setwd(folder)
nsim <- 50

setwd("your_working_directory")
getwd()

# ---- 1. Load data and standardize covariates ----

# Load and organize data
final <- read.csv("data.csv")
final$Est_log <- log(final$Est)
final[is.na(final)] <- 0
final$Year <- str_sub(final$uniqueID, -4)
final <- final %>%
  filter(Layer == "est")

# Add a column for bird name (uniqueID without the year)
final$name <- sub("_.*$", "", final$uniqueID)
table(final$name)

# How many unique birds are there?
unique(final$name)

# Standardize covariates: subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation
final <- final %>% mutate(
  Roads_normalized_s = (Roads_normalized - mean(Roads_normalized)) / sd(Roads_normalized),
  CC_Mean_s          = (CC_mean - mean(CC_mean)) / sd(CC_mean),
  CC_stdev_s         = (CC_stdev - mean(CC_stdev)) / sd(CC_stdev),
  Herb_Crop_s        = (Herb_Crop - mean(Herb_Crop)) / sd(Herb_Crop),
  Nat_Herb_s         = (Nat_Herb - mean(Nat_Herb)) / sd(Nat_Herb),
  Days_used_s        = (Days_used - mean(Days_used)) / sd(Days_used),
  Points_s           = (Points - mean(Points)) / sd(Points)
)
```

## Models by ecoregion

```{r models}
# ---- 2. Subset data by ecoregion ----

# Open ecoregion only
final_open <- final %>%
  filter(Ecosystem_condensed == "Open")
sum(final$Ecosystem_condensed == "Open")

# Forested ecoregions only (Mixed Forests and Northern Boreal)
final_forested <- final %>%
  filter(Ecosystem_condensed %in% c("Mixed Forests", "Northern Boreal"))

# Open and forested combined, with forested ecoregions grouped together
final_open_forested <- final %>%
  mutate(Ecoregion_grouped = case_when(
    Ecosystem_condensed %in% c("Forest", "Taiga") ~ "Forested",
    TRUE ~ Ecosystem_condensed
  ))

# ---- 3. Mixed effects models ----
# Each model below overwrites `mod`; the last one run is used for the CIs and
# predictions that follow.

# Test for effects of longitude
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Longitude + (1 | name), data = final)

# All covariates together (to test for collinearity)
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Roads_normalized_s + CC_Mean_s + CC_stdev_s +
              Herb_Crop_s + Nat_Herb_s + Ecosystem_condensed + (1 | name),
            data = final)

check_collinearity(mod)

# Forested ecoregions
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Roads_normalized_s + Sex + CC_Mean_s + CC_stdev_s +
              Herb_Crop_s + Nat_Herb_s + (1 | name),
            data = final_forested)

# Sex interactions
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Nat_Herb_s * Sex + (1 | name), data = final)

# Open ecoregion (swap in each covariate individually and rerun)
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Herb_Crop_s + (1 | name), data = final_open)

# Differences among ecoregions
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Ecosystem_condensed + Sex + (1 | name), data = final)

emmeans(mod, pairwise ~ Ecosystem_condensed)

# Total points and days used
mod <- lmer(Est_log ~ Sex + Points_s + Days_used_s + (1 | name), data = final)

# Check correlation between points and days used
cor(final$Points, final$Days_used, use = "complete.obs")

# Plot home range size against total days used
ggplot(final, aes(x = Days_used, y = Est_log)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

# Plot home range size against total points
ggplot(final, aes(x = Points, y = Est_log)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

# Model fit: R-squared, residual normality, and collinearity
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(object = mod)
qqnorm(resid(mod))
check_collinearity(mod)

# ---- 4. Confidence intervals ----

# Bootstrap the fixed effects estimates with bootMer
simsCI <- bootMer(mod, FUN = fixef, nsim = 500)
dim(simsCI$t)  # 500 bootstrap estimates for each fixed effect
# View(simsCI$t)
apply(simsCI$t, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))  # 95% CIs on the coefficients

# Organize CIs for the manuscript table
CIs <- apply(simsCI$t, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))
estimates <- data.frame(Covariate = colnames(simsCI$t),
                        Mean      = round(fixef(mod), 2),
                        Lower95   = round(CIs[1, ], 2),
                        Upper95   = round(CIs[2, ], 2))

estimates
```

## Effect plot for forested ecoregions

```{r forest-effects-plot}
# Effect estimates for all forested ecoregions (Mixed Forests and Northern Boreal)
effects <- data.frame(
  Covariate = c("Intercept",
                "Sex (M)",
                "Roads",
                "Canopy Cover Mean",
                "Canopy Cover SD",
                "Herbaceous Croplands",
                "Natural Herbaceous"),
  Mean    = c(0.3, 1.92, -0.38, 0.07, 0.34, -0.39, 0.1),
  Lower95 = c(-0.1, 1.39, -0.62, -0.31, 0.01, -0.86, -0.31),
  Upper95 = c(0.71, 2.39, -0.16, 0.38, 0.71, 0.09, 0.52)
)

# Order covariates from top to bottom
effects$Covariate <- factor(
  effects$Covariate,
  levels = rev(effects$Covariate)
)

pdf(file = "Forested_all_variables.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

forest_plot <- ggplot(effects, aes(x = Mean, y = Covariate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Lower95, xmax = Upper95),
                 height = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Effects for Forested Ecoregions",
    x = "Effect estimate (95% CI)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )

ggsave("forest_effects.pdf", plot = forest_plot,
       width = 7, height = 5, units = "in")
```

## Predictions for plotting

```{r predictions}
# Covariates needed: roads and canopy cover SD (forested), herbaceous croplands
# (open), and natural herbaceous (forested)

# ---- 5. Generate predictions for plotting ----

nsim <- 50

# To make a plot, we give the model a series of x values and have it predict
# y values. As with the fixed effects estimates above, mean predictions are
# easy, but uncertainty is more complicated, so we use bootMer again to get
# CIs on the predictions.

# Sequences of standardized covariate values to predict over
x.CC_stdev <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_stdev_s),
                  to = quantile(final_forested$CC_stdev_s, probs = 0.95),
                  length.out = nsim)

x.herb_crop <- seq(from = min(final_open$Herb_Crop_s),
                   to = max(final_open$Herb_Crop_s),
                   length.out = nsim)
x.nat_herb <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Nat_Herb_s),
                  to = max(final_forested$Nat_Herb_s),
                  length.out = nsim)
x.CC_mean <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_Mean_s),
                 to = max(final_forested$CC_Mean_s),
                 length.out = nsim)

x.Roads_normalized_s <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s),
                            to = max(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s),
                            length.out = nsim)

# Datasets for prediction: vary one covariate and hold all others at their
# means. Because the covariates are standardized, their means are 0.
new.data.CC_stdev <- data.frame(Sex                = "M",
                                Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                CC_Mean_s          = 0,
                                CC_stdev_s         = x.CC_stdev,
                                Herb_Crop_s        = 0,
                                Nat_Herb_s         = 0)

new.data.herb_crop <- data.frame(Sex                = "M",
                                 Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                 CC_Mean_s          = 0,
                                 CC_stdev_s         = 0,
                                 Herb_Crop_s        = x.herb_crop,
                                 Nat_Herb_s         = 0)

new.data.nat_herb <- data.frame(Sex                = "M",
                                Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                                CC_Mean_s          = 0,
                                CC_stdev_s         = 0,
                                Herb_Crop_s        = 0,
                                Nat_Herb_s         = x.nat_herb)

new.data.CC_mean <- data.frame(Sex                = "M",
                               Roads_normalized_s = 0,
                               CC_Mean_s          = x.CC_mean,
                               CC_stdev_s         = 0,
                               Herb_Crop_s        = 0,
                               Nat_Herb_s         = 0)

new.data.Roads_normalized <- data.frame(Sex                = "M",
                                        Roads_normalized_s = x.Roads_normalized_s,
                                        CC_Mean_s          = 0,
                                        CC_stdev_s         = 0,
                                        Herb_Crop_s        = 0,
                                        Nat_Herb_s         = 0)

# Mean predictions (see ?predict.merMod for details)
?predict.merMod

pred.CC_stdev <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form = NA,
                         newdata = new.data.CC_stdev)
pred.herb_crop <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form = NA,
                          newdata = new.data.herb_crop)
pred.nat_herb <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form = NA,
                         newdata = new.data.nat_herb)
pred.CC_mean <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form = NA,
                        newdata = new.data.CC_mean)
pred.Roads_normalized <- predict(mod, type = "response", re.form = NA,
                                 newdata = new.data.Roads_normalized)

# Bootstrapped confidence intervals on the predictions
CI.CC_stdev <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim,
                       FUN = function(x) {
                         predict(x, newdata = new.data.CC_stdev,
                                 type = "response", re.form = NA)
                       })

CI.herb_crop <- bootMer(mod,
                        nsim = nsim,
                        FUN = function(x) {
                          predict(x, newdata = new.data.herb_crop,
                                  type = "response", re.form = NA)
                        })

CI.nat_herb <- bootMer(mod,
                       nsim = nsim,
                       FUN = function(x) {
                         predict(x, newdata = new.data.nat_herb,
                                 type = "response", re.form = NA)
                       })

CI.CC_mean <- bootMer(mod,
                      nsim = nsim,
                      FUN = function(x) {
                        predict(x, newdata = new.data.CC_mean,
                                type = "response", re.form = NA)
                      })

CI.Roads_normalized <- bootMer(mod,
                               nsim = nsim,
                               FUN = function(x) {
                                 predict(x, newdata = new.data.Roads_normalized,
                                         type = "response", re.form = NA)
                               })

# ---- 6. Covariate sequences on the original (unstandardized) scale ----
# These match the standardized sequences above and are used for the x axes.
# Base R plotting is used below, but ggplot would work too.

x.CC_stdev.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_stdev),
                      to = quantile(final_forested$CC_stdev, probs = 0.95),
                      length.out = nsim)
x.herb_crop.raw <- seq(from = min(final_open$Herb_Crop),
                       to = max(final_open$Herb_Crop),
                       length.out = nsim)
x.nat_herb.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Nat_Herb),
                      to = max(final_forested$Nat_Herb),
                      length.out = nsim)
x.CC_mean.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$CC_Mean),
                     to = max(final_forested$CC_Mean),
                     length.out = nsim)

x.Roads_normalized.raw <- seq(from = min(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s),
                              to = max(final_forested$Roads_normalized_s),
                              length.out = nsim)
```

## Plotting

```{r plotting}
# ---- 7. Prediction plots, y axis on the log scale ----
# Multi-panel plot with herbaceous croplands in the top left panel

pdf(file = "Forested_all_variables.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 1, 1), tcl = 0.3, mgp = c(1.5, 0.2, 0),
    las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.8)

# Herbaceous croplands
plot(x = x.herb_crop.raw, y = pred.herb_crop, ylim = c(0, 3.3), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "% cover herbaceous croplands", ylab = "log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.herb_crop.raw, rev(x.herb_crop.raw)),
        c(apply(CI.herb_crop$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(CI.herb_crop$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.herb_crop.raw, y = pred.herb_crop, col = "black", lwd = 2)

# Skip the top right panel
plot.new()

# Natural herbaceous
plot(x = x.nat_herb.raw, y = pred.nat_herb, ylim = c(0, 3.3), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "% cover natural herbaceous", ylab = "log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.nat_herb.raw, rev(x.nat_herb.raw)),
        c(apply(CI.nat_herb$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(CI.nat_herb$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.nat_herb.raw, y = pred.nat_herb, col = "black", lwd = 2)

# Standard deviation of canopy cover
plot(x = x.CC_stdev.raw, y = pred.CC_stdev, ylim = c(0, 3.3), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "Standard deviation of canopy cover", ylab = "log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.CC_stdev.raw, rev(x.CC_stdev.raw)),
        c(apply(CI.CC_stdev$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(CI.CC_stdev$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.CC_stdev.raw, y = pred.CC_stdev, col = "black", lwd = 2)

dev.off()

# Mean canopy cover
plot(x = x.CC_mean.raw, y = pred.CC_mean, ylim = c(0, 3.3), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "Canopy cover Mean", ylab = "log (Home range size)")
polygon(c(x.CC_mean.raw, rev(x.CC_mean.raw)),
        c(apply(CI.CC_mean$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(CI.CC_mean$t, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#900C3F80", border = NA)
lines(x = x.CC_mean.raw, y = pred.CC_mean, col = "black", lwd = 2)

# ---- 8. Prediction plots, y axis on the data scale (not log scale) ----

pdf(file = "plot_all.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 1, 1), tcl = 0.3, mgp = c(1.5, 0.2, 0),
    las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.8)

# Make it narrower
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(3, 4, 1, 2), tcl = 0.3, mgp = c(1.5, 0.2, 0),
    las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.8)

pdf(file = "herb_crop_open.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

# Herbaceous croplands (open)
plot(x = x.herb_crop.raw, y = exp(pred.herb_crop), ylim = c(0, 23), cex.main = 0.8,
     xlim = c(0, 100), bty = "l", type = "n", main = "Herb Cropland for Open",
     xlab = "% cover herbaceous croplands", ylab = "Home range size (ha)")
polygon(c(x.herb_crop.raw, rev(x.herb_crop.raw)),
        c(apply(exp(CI.herb_crop$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(exp(CI.herb_crop$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#B02526", border = NA)
lines(x = x.herb_crop.raw, y = exp(pred.herb_crop), col = "black", lwd = 2)

dev.off()

getwd()

# Natural herbaceous
plot(x = x.nat_herb.raw, y = exp(pred.nat_herb), ylim = c(0, 23), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "% cover natural herbaceous", ylab = "Home range size (ha)")
polygon(c(x.nat_herb.raw, rev(x.nat_herb.raw)),
        c(apply(exp(CI.nat_herb$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(exp(CI.nat_herb$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#B02526", border = NA)
lines(x = x.nat_herb.raw, y = exp(pred.nat_herb), col = "black", lwd = 2)

# Standard deviation of canopy cover (forested)
pdf(file = "cc_stdev_forested.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

plot(x = x.CC_stdev.raw, y = exp(pred.CC_stdev), ylim = c(0, 23), bty = "l", type = "n",
     cex.main = 0.8, xlab = "Standard deviation of canopy cover",
     ylab = "Home range size (ha)", main = "Canopy Cover stdev for Forested")
polygon(c(x.CC_stdev.raw, rev(x.CC_stdev.raw)),
        c(apply(exp(CI.CC_stdev$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(exp(CI.CC_stdev$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#B02526", border = NA)
lines(x = x.CC_stdev.raw, y = exp(pred.CC_stdev), col = "black", lwd = 2)

dev.off()

# Mean canopy cover (forested)
pdf("SD_forested2.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)

plot(x = x.CC_mean.raw, y = exp(pred.CC_mean), ylim = c(0, 23), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "Mean Canopy Cover", ylab = "Home range size (ha)")
polygon(c(x.CC_mean.raw, rev(x.CC_mean.raw)),
        c(apply(exp(CI.CC_mean$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(exp(CI.CC_mean$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#B02526", border = NA)
lines(x = x.CC_mean.raw, y = exp(pred.CC_mean), col = "black", lwd = 2)

dev.off()

# Roads (forested)
pdf("Roads_forested.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)

plot(x = x.Roads_normalized.raw, y = exp(pred.Roads_normalized), cex.main = 0.8,
     ylim = c(0, 23), bty = "l", type = "n",
     xlab = "Mean Road Value", ylab = "Home range size (ha)",
     main = "Roads for Forested Ecoregion")
polygon(c(x.Roads_normalized.raw, rev(x.Roads_normalized.raw)),
        c(apply(exp(CI.Roads_normalized$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rev(apply(exp(CI.Roads_normalized$t), 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))),
        col = "#B02526", border = NA)
lines(x = x.Roads_normalized.raw, y = exp(pred.Roads_normalized), col = "black", lwd = 2)

getwd()

# ---- 9. Home range size by ecoregion ----

pdf("ecoregions_violin3.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)

ggplot(final, aes(x = Ecosystem_condensed, y = Est)) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_sina(
    aes(color = Sex),
    size = 3,
    alpha = 0.8,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.15)
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  ) +
  ylab("95% AKDE Home Range Size (km^2)")

dev.off()

# ---- 10. Effect estimates plot ----

ggplot(results, aes(x = Mean, y = Covariate)) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = Lower_95_CI, xmax = Upper_95_CI),
    height = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Effect estimate",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
